title: A tetranuclear holmium compound exhibiting single molecule magnet behavior

material_class.structural_family: planar butterfly Ho4 core with two μ3-OH and six phenoxide bridges

synthesis.procedure: The Schiff base ligand H2L was prepared by the reported procedure. Triethylamine (0.2 mmol) was added at room temperature to a stirring solution of Ho(NO3)3·6H2O (0.1 mmol, 0.0459 g), H2L (0.1 mmol, 0.0243 g) and sodium pivalate (0.1 mmol, 0.0142 g) in MeOH (10 mL) and MeCN (10 mL), giving a turbid yellow solution. After stirring for 2 h, the yellow precipitate was collected by filtration and washed with cold MeOH. The residue was recrystallized from DMF, giving a bright yellow solution that was left undisturbed to concentrate by slow evaporation. X-ray quality crystals of 1 grew over 4 days, were collected by filtration, washed with cold DMF, and dried under air.
synthesis.temperature: room temperature (reaction); slow evaporation for crystallization
synthesis.time: stirred 2 h; crystals grew over 4 days
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution reaction followed by filtration and recrystallization from DMF by slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Yellow precipitate filtered and washed with cold MeOH; residue recrystallized from DMF and left undisturbed to evaporate. Crystals collected by filtration, washed with cold DMF, and dried in air.

properties.summary: Compound 1 is a tetranuclear butterfly Ho4 cluster that shows field-induced slow relaxation of magnetization and SMM behavior. Zero-field ac data show only weak frequency dependence below 10 K, attributed to QTM; under 5 kOe a clear frequency-dependent χ'/χ'' response appears. Arrhenius fitting gives ΔE/kB = 21.49 K and τ0 = 6.97×10^-7 s. Dc χmT is close to four uncoupled HoIII ions at room temperature and magnetization at 2 K remains unsaturated.
